(basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He also represents the senior [[Italian national basketball team|Italian national team]]. He mainly plays at the [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] position, but he has also played at [[center (basketball)|center]]. Melli earned an [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]] selection in [[2016–17 EuroLeague|2017]]. ==Youth career== The [[Reggio Emilia]] native started his career with home town side [[Pallacanestro Reggiana]]. After an accumulation of injuries Melli was called up to train with the senior team in October 2004, at only 13. He sat on the bench during a 24 October league game (an age record) though he did not play and returned to the youth teams afterwards.{{cite web Emotional |archive-date=8 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160308180324/http://ricerca.gelocal.it/gazzettadireggio/archivio/gazzettadireggio/2006/10/26/ES4PO_ES402.html |url-status=dead }} ==Professional career== ===Pallacanestro Reggiana (2007–2010)=== In August 2007, he signed a five-year professional contract with Pallacanestro Reggiana and started training with the first team.{{cite web |url=http://www.pallacanestroreggiana.it/pagina.php?id=2671&n=Melli,%20accordo%20quinquennale |title=Melli, accordo quinquennale |author= |date=11 August 2007 |website=[[Pallacanestro Reggiana|PallacanestroReggiana]].it |access-date=19 July 2015 |language=it |trans-title=Melli, five-year deal}} The same year, in October, the 16-year-old debuted in the [[Italian basketball league system|Italian national second division]] [[Serie A2 Basket|LegaDue]]. In May 2008, during the [[promotion and relegation|promotion]] semi-finals against [[Aurora Basket Jesi]], he replaced injured starter [[Benjamin Ortner]] and contributed 16 points and 15 rebounds in a losing effort. He finished the season playing an average of 10.6 minutes with 3.4 points and 2.9 rebounds.{{cite web |url=http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/gameCent/p/leagueid/SUI/ot/1/pid/6031587/season/2008/tid/6000009/tidstat//playerView.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305174911/http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/gameCent/p/leagueid/SUI/ot/1/pid/6031587/season/2008/tid/6000009/tidstat//playerView.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=5 March 2016 |title=Nicolò Melli – Season 2007/2008 |author= |website=[[FIBA]].com |access-date=19 July 2015}}{{cite web |url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2010/luglio/02/Nicolo_Melli_Testa_tecnica_Ecco_ga_3_100702021.shtml?refresh_ce-cp |title=Nicolò Melli Testa e tecnica Ecco il futuro di Milano |last=Barilli |first=Daniele |date=2 July 2010 |website=[[La Gazzetta dello Sport|Gazzetta]].it |location=Reggio Emilia |access-date=20 July 2015 |language=it |trans-title=Nicolò Melli. Brains and technique. Here's Milan's future}} During the off-season, the 17-year-old participated in the Reebok Eurocamp in [[Treviso]] but did not make an impression on observers (albeit playing against older players, sometimes by five years).{{cite web |url=http://www.draftexpress.com/article/2008-Reebok-Eurocamp-in-Treviso,-Days-Three-and-Four-2921/ |title=2008 Reebok Eurocamp in Treviso, Days Three and Four |last1=Fernández |first1=Luis |last2=Givony |first2=Johnathan |date= 10 June 2008 |website=DraftExpress.com |access-date=21 July 2015}} He also returned to the U.S., attending the Adidas Nations that pitted international teams of promising youngsters. Though he was praised by an observer for his work ethic, it was also noted that his game (and lack of athleticism) was unsuited to the American game.{{cite web |url=http://www.nbadraft.net/2008-adidas-nations-camp-top-prospects |title=2008 adidas Nations Camp: Top Prospects |last=Smith |first=Aran |date=20 August 2008 |website=NBADraft.net |access-date=30 July 2015}} Melli started the next season in great form, with 12 points and 18 rebounds followed by 24 points in two games, however, on 21 December 2008, Melli suffered a serious knee injury. Scans revealed an [[anterior cruciate ligament injury]] on his left knee, requiring surgery and at least five months of rehabilitation though he would be able to continue his career.{{cite web |url=http://www.pallacanestroreggiana.it/2143/Forza-e-coraggio-Nicol%26ograve%3B! |title=Forza e coraggio Nicolò! |author= |date=22 December 2008 |website=[[Pallacanestro Reggiana]].it |access-date=19 2010 |website=[[Gazzetta di Reggio|GazzettadiReggio]].it |access-date=20 July 2015 |language=it |trans-title=Season over for Melli, the team on the market}} ===Olimpia Milano (2010–2015)=== ====2010–11 season==== On the radar of strong sides for some time, Melli joined [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|Armani Jeans Milano]], of the elite domestic [[Lega Basket Serie A|Serie A]] and European [[EuroLeague]] in July 2010, signing a four-year deal.{{cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/73631/armani-jeans-milano-tabs-top-prospect-melli |title=Armani Jeans Milano tabs top prospect Melli |last=Petitti |first=Romano |date=10 July 2010 |website=[[EuroLeague]].net |location=Milan |access-date=20 July 2015}} After struggling to earn minutes, Melli was [[loan (sports)|loaned]] to fellow Serie A side [[Victoria Libertas Pesaro|Scavolini-Siviglia Pesaro]] in February 2011.{{cite web |url=http://www.corrieredellosport.it/basket/serie_a/2011/02/16-156134/Melli,+ufficiale%C2%A0il+prestito+a+Pesaro |title=Melli, è ufficiale il prestito a Pesaro |author= |date=16 February 2011 |website=[[Corriere dello Sport – Stadio|CorrieredelloSport]].it |location=Milan |access-date=20 July 2015 |language=it |trans-title=Melli, the loan to Pesaro is official}} A month later he returned to Milan, to take part in the [[Lega Basket All Star Game|Italian All Star Game]] where he contributed 12 points for Italy.{{cite web |url=https://it.eurosport.yahoo.com/14032011/45/serie-questa-si-italia-rimonta.html |title=Serie A – Questa sì che è una Italia da rimonta! |last=Fantini |first=Daniele |date=13 March 2011 |website=[[Eurosport]].it |access-date=20 July 2015 |language=it |trans-title=Serie A – This is for sure a comeback Italy}} Melli finished the [[2010–11 Lega Basket Serie A|2010–11 season]] with 3.8 points, 3.3 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 16 minutes per game for Pesaro (compared with 9 minutes for Milan previously).{{cite web |url=http://195.56.77.208/player/pbd.phtml?ply=MEL-NIC-91&from=1980&team=1257&type2=t&name_search=Melli |title=Melli, Nicolò – Statistiche individuali |author= |website=[[Lega Basket Serie A|LegaBasket]].it |access-date=20 July 2015 |language=it |trans-title=Melli, Nicolò – Individual statistics}} ====2011–12 season==== The next season saw Melli accrue slightly more playing time but despite some highlights, such as a team-high 17 points in a [[Euroleague 2011–12 Top 16 Group G|EuroLeague Group G]] defeat against [[BC UNICS|UNICS Kazan]], he finished the regular season with 3.4 points and 2.7 rebounds in 11 minutes per game (Serie A) and 3.8 points and 1.9 rebounds in 9 minutes per game (EuroLeague).{{cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=002849&seasoncode=E2011 |title=Melli, Nicolo – 2011–2012 Statistics |author= |website=[[EuroLeague]].net |access-date=21 July 2015}} He had more impact in the [[2011–12 Lega Basket Serie A#Play-offs|Serie A playoffs]], including decisive performances in the semi-final game 3 against former side Pesaro (5 points in 19 minutes and a good defensive performance, with 7 rebounds, 2 steals and 1 block){{cite web |url=http://www.repubblica.it/sport/basket/2012/06/04/news/milano_vince_pesaro_gara_4-36555444/ |title=Milano ritrova Fotsis e la finale. Ma Pesaro s'arrende all'ultimo minuto |last=Valenti |first=Stefano |date=4 June 2012 |website=[[la Repubblica|Repubblica]].it |access-date=21 July 2015 |location=Pesaro |language=it |trans-title=Milan finds Fotsis and the final again. But Pesaro surrendered [only] in the end}} and then in game 4 of the finals against future champions [[Mens Sana 1871 Basket|Montepaschi Siena]] where he was part of a second-half fightback to win the game, finishing with 11 points and 4 rebounds in 13 minutes.{{cite web |url=https://it.eurosport.yahoo.com/17062012/45/serie-basket-milano-rabbia-serie-resta-viva.html |title=Serie A Basket – Milano di rabbia, la serie resta viva |author= |date=15 June 2012 |website=[[Eurosport]].it |location=Milan |access-date=21 July 2015 |language=it |trans-title=Serie A Basketball – Milan in anger, the series stays alive}} ====2012–13 season==== In 2012–13, Melli increased his averages to 5.8 points and 4.1 rebounds (Serie A), 4.6 points and 3 rebounds (EuroLeague), and his minutes to respectively 17 and 15 in a season nearly devoid of highlights both personally and for Milan (eliminated in the [[2012–13 Lega Basket Serie A#Playoffs|domestic quarterfinals]] and the [[Euroleague 2012–13 Regular Season Group C|EuroLeague regular season]]).{{cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=002849&seasoncode=E2012 |title=Melli, Nicolo – 2012–2013 Statistics |author= |website=[[EuroLeague]].net |access-date=21 July 2015}} An exception was his third successive participation in the December Italian league All-Star Game, in which he top-scored along with Milan teammate [[Alessandro Gentile]] (18 points), adding a game-best 10 rebounds.{{cite web |url=http://www.olimpiamilano.com/gentile-e-melli-leoncini-olimpia-super-in-azzurro/ |title=Gentile e Melli, leoncini Olimpia super in azzurro |author= |date=16 December 2012 |website=[[Olimpia Milano]].com |access-date=21 July 2015 |language=it |trans-title=Gentile and Melli, Olimpia young lions great in blue}} During the summer, he worked out with a number of [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] sides, with an observer commenting that he seemed too light physically for the league, he would go undrafted in the [[2013 NBA draft]].{{cite web |url=http://www.csnwashington.com/basketball-washington-wizards/talk/clanton-could-be-sleeper-wizards |title=Clanton could be a sleeper for Wizards 2013 |website=[[Star Tribune|StarTribune]].com |location=Minneapolis |access-date=20 July 2015}}{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/draft/2013/workout-130625 |title=Workouts – Bucks Draft 2013 |author= |date=24 June 2013 |website=[[NBA]].com |publisher=[[Milwaukee Bucks]] |access-date=20 July 2015}}{{cite web |url=http://www.mlive.com/pistons/index.ssf/2013/06/detroit_pistons_release_list_o.html |title=Detroit Pistons release list of 2013 NBA Draft prospects who worked out for them this week |last=Mayo |first=David |date=27 June 2013 |website=Mlive.com |publisher=[[Advance Digital]] |location=Auburn Hills |access-date=20 July 2015}} ====2013–14 season==== 2013–14 proved to be Melli's breakthrough season, with his good performances becoming more regular as he cemented his place in Milan's starting five.{{cite web |url=http://www.olimpiamilano.com/red-shoes-are-back-26-nick-melli/ |title=Red Shoes Are Back 26: Nick Melli |author= |date=14 July 2014 |website=[[Olimpia Milano|OlimpiaMilano]].com |access-date=28 July 2015 |language=it}} The first of those decisive contributions came in Milan's second EuroLeague game of the season against [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris]], where Melli scored a career-high 20 points, adding 9 rebounds and 2 steals in 25 minutes to earn a [[Performance Index Rating|PIR]] of 28.{{cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=17&seasoncode=E2013#!report |title=Melli stars for EA7 Milan in victory over Zalgiris |author= |date=24 October 2014 |website=[[EuroLeague]].net |access-date=28 July 2015}} During the decisive 74–73 victory against [[Brose Bamberg]] in the penultimate group stage game, he defended [[Zack Wright|Wright]] as he missed the Brose's last shot which allowed Milan to progress to the Top 16. Though he lad less impact further on as Milan reached the [[2013–14 Euroleague#Quarter-finals|EuroLeague quarterfinals]], Melli finished with respectable averages of 5.3 points, 4.3 rebounds, 0.8 assists and 0.9 steals in around 21 minutes in the competition.{{cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=002849&seasoncode=E2013 |title=Melli, Nicolo – 2013–2014 Statistics |author= |website=[[EuroLeague]].net |access-date=29 July 2015}} Domestically, he regularly posted scored in double figures, including a career-high 24 points against [[Pallacanestro Virtus Roma|Roma]], put against more average games he finished with 6.9 points and 4.9 rebounds in a career-high 21 minutes. Discarding the statistics, Melli had crucial contributions during the [[2013–14 Lega Basket Serie A#Play-offs|Serie A playoffs]], starting with 18 points in 22 minutes in the first game against [[Pistoia Basket 2000|Pistoia]]. After starting the finals series against defending champions [[Mens Sana 1871 Basket|Montepaschi Siena]] with some off-games Melli exploded in the final two games. In the do-or-die game 6, with Milan trailing, he scored two successive three-pointers to regain the lead before adding a steal and a number of decisive rebounds as Milan won the game to earn a game 7 decider.{{cite web |url=http://www.olimpiamilano.com/scheda-partita/montepaschi-siena-vs-ea7-armani-milano-gara-6-72-74/ |title=Montepaschi Siena vs. EA7 Armani Milano (gara 6) 72–74 |author= |website=[[Olimpia Milano|OlimpiaMilano]].com |access-date=30 July 2015 |language=it |trans-title=Montepaschi Siena vs. EA7 Armani Milano (game 6) 72–74}} In that game, he contributed 11 points and a career-high 13 rebounds as Milan won to become Italian champions for the first time in 18 years.{{cite web |url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/coid_XsEFNa7dGBwCn8qtjld6a2.articleMode_on.html |title=Olimpia Milano 18-year wait |author= |date=30 June 2014 |website=[[FIBA Europe|FIBAEurope]].com |access-date=30 July 2015}} ====2014–15 season==== In July 2014, his contract with Milan was extended for another year.{{cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/139720/ea7-emporio-armani-melli-together-one-more-year |title=EA7 Emporio Armani, Melli together one more year |author= |date=18 July 2014 |website=[[EuroLeague]] |access-date=20 July 2015}} The season proved more difficult for both parties, Melli had an unremarkable season (5.3 points and 3.5 rebounds in the EuroLeague, 5.6 and 4.3 in Serie A) as Milan were stopped in the [[2014–15 Lega Basket Serie A#Playoffs 2|Italian playoff semi-finals]] in their title defense and stalled in the [[2014–15 Euroleague#Top 16|EuroLeague Top 16]].{{cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/679ufolmvt4e7i4f/brose-baskets-signs-forward-melli |title=Brose Baskets signs forward Melli |author= |date=14 July 2015 |website=[[EuroLeague]].net |access-date=14 July 2015}} ===Brose Bamberg (2015–2017)=== Melli moved abroad in July 2015, signing with German side Brose Bamberg for two years. He cited Brose's strong pursuit of his services and their offering him a more important role in the side as motivation for the move abroad, adding that the presence of compatriots [[Andrea Trinchieri]] and [[Daniele Baiesi]] as [[head coach|head]] [[basketball coach|coach]] and [[general manager (basketball)|GM]] respectively would facilitate his adaptation.{{cite web |url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Basket/Eurolega/24-07-2015/basket-eurolega-melli-sfida-tedesca-voglio-ruolo-diverso-120681574936.shtml?refresh_ce-cp |title=Basket, Eurolega: Melli, la sfida tedesca "Voglio un ruolo diverso" |last=Chiabotti |first=Luca |date=24 July 2014 |website= [[La Gazzetta dello Sport|Gazzetta]].it |location=Milan |access-date=30 July 2015 |language=it |trans-title=Basketball, Euroleague: Melli, the German challenge. “I want a different role”}} Melli was named the [[EuroLeague MVP of the Month|MVP of the Month of November]] of the [[2015–16 Euroleague]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/6ig4qo6j6cno4hvo|title=MVP for November: Nicolo Melli, Brose Baskets Bamberg}} Melli was named the [[EuroLeague MVP of the Round|EuroLeague Round 11 MVP]], after scoring 27 points and grabbing 14 rebounds, in a 70–85 away victory over [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], on 8 December 2016.{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/7go4c6rivk8facvx/regular-season-round-11-mvp-nicolo-melli-brose-bamberg|title=Regular Season Round 11 MVP: Nicolo Melli, Brose Bamberg|publisher=EuroLeague|date=12 December 2016}} He was named to the season's [[All-EuroLeague Second Team]].[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/7svd7bevhvxpms6h The 2016–17 All-EuroLeague Team presented by 7DAYS!] ===Fenerbahçe (2017–2019)=== On 8 July 2017, Melli signed a three-year contract with Turkish club [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe]].{{cite news|title=Fenerbahce adds All-EuroLeague forward Melli to the mix|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/7vln5d3dhb9w8sky/fenerbahce-adds-all-euroleague-forward-melli-to-the-mix|access-date=8 July 2017|work=Euroleague.net|date=8 July 2017}} In the [[2017–18 EuroLeague]] season, Fenerbahçe made it to the [[2018 EuroLeague Final Four]], its fourth consecutive [[EuroLeague Final Four|Final Four]] appearance. Eventually, they lost to [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]], by a score of 80–85 in the finals game. In the finals game, Melli was [[EuroLeague Finals Top Scorer|the finals top scorer]], as he scored 28 points, which was the most points scored in a EuroLeague Finals game by a player since 1985.{{cite news|title=Real Madrid is 2018 EuroLeague champion|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=260&seasoncode=E2017#!report|access-date=20 May 2018|work=euroleague.net|date=20 May 2018}} He had a season-best performance in the [[EuroLeague Finals]], scoring 28 points and grabbing 6 rebounds. Over 36 EuroLeague games played in total, he averaged 8.9 points, 5 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game. ===New Orleans Pelicans (2019–2021)=== On 25 July 2019, Melli signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign Nicolò Melli|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-sign-nicolo-melli|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=26 July 2019|date=25 July 2019}} On 22 October 2019, Melli made his debut in NBA, coming off the bench in a 122–130 overtime loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]] with fourteen points, five rebounds and two assists.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160623|title=VanVleet scores career-high 34, Raptors top Pelicans 130–122|date=22 October 2019|publisher=ESPN|access-date=22 October 2019}} On 12 February 2020, Melli replaced [[Deandre Ayton]] for the World Team in the [[Rising Stars Challenge]].{{cite news|title=New Orleans' Melli to replace Phoenix's Ayton in 2020 NBA Rising Stars|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2020/02/13/melli-replaces-ayton-rising-stars-official-release|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=13 for [[James Johnson (basketball, born 1987)|James Johnson]] and [[Wes Iwundu]], in addition to a second-round draft-pick.{{cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavsgetredickintrade/|title=Mavs acquire sharpshooting guard Redick in trade with Pelicans|work=mavs.com|date=26 March 2021}} He made his debut three days later, in a 127–106 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] where he recorded six Enrico, Melli's younger brother who was born in 1995, has also played basketball for Reggiana.{{cite web |url=http://journalstar.com/sports/local/olympic-volleyball-roots-grew-in-palmyra/article_4351c36a-dcec-58ab-8c5b-45fefa3c0f28.html |title=Olympic volleyball roots grew in Palmyra |last=Bamesberger |first=Michael |date=6 August 2012 |website=[[Lincoln Journal Star]] |access-date=20 July 2015}} Melli has dual citizenship in Italy and the United States.
